registered_before: any candidate was built or any tuning game was played
why_opponents_and_not_seeds: The engine cannot be seeded, so a seed-level split is not available; but even if it were, it would hold out the wrong thing. With cheap games and a mutation loop, the failure mode is fitting the quirks of a handful of rule-based opponents, and only a split by OPPONENT IDENTITY detects that. Every tuning decision in this contract is made on the dev panel alone.

rationale.pub_tetsutani_grimmsnarl: stands in for ~60% of the 1000+ ladder bands; the single most important matchup and the champion's worst (0.250)
rationale.pub_jazivxt_codex_alakazam: the Alakazam archetype, ~10-27% depending on band
rationale.official_iono: an official sample, and the champion's best matchup -- included so a change that trades away a good matchup is visible
rationale.official_mega_abomasnow: an official sample with a different plan shape
rationale.official_dragapult: the mirror; a challenger that only beats its own parent is winning nothing

rationale.archetype_holdout: NO search-based Mega Lucario implementation appears on the dev panel, and both validation Lucario agents are of that kind -- so an improvement that only works against the agents it was tuned on will fail here
rationale.implementation_holdout: two further Alakazam implementations (rising_tide, raunakdey) distinct from the dev-panel one, so 'beats Alakazam' has to generalise across implementations
rationale.pub_makthanithin_lucario_1084: the strongest publicly-attested agent available here (its author's kernel is titled with a 1084.5 leaderboard score)

validation_panel.rule: No candidate is selected, ranked, promoted or killed on validation-panel evidence. It is read once per branch, after the dev-panel decision has already been made.

final_holdout.rule: The final panel runs every player, at the largest game count the remaining time allows, and is run ONCE per finalist. It reports the number; it does not choose the finalist.

scores_reported.field_off_mirror: unweighted mean of per-opponent score rates, excluding the mirror. The primary number.
scores_reported.field_ladder_weighted: the same rates weighted by public-ladder archetype usage (META_REPORT §2). Secondary, and never used alone -- the usage shares are a third-party two-day-old snapshot with wide band-level uncertainty.

promotion_rule.screen: dev panel, >= 400 games per candidate; keep only candidates whose dev field score point estimate exceeds the champion's
promotion_rule.confirm: dev panel, >= 1000 games, on survivors only
promotion_rule.promote_if: a material broad-field improvement (~+4 points is the target, not a threshold) that survives on the validation panel with no catastrophic matchup (no opponent below 0.15) and no regression in errors, timeouts or illegal actions
promotion_rule.note: Smaller gains may still be retained when precise and strategically important -- e.g. a gain concentrated in the Grimmsnarl matchup, which is 60% of the top ladder bands.
